clue.text: Fat parrot talking with extra capacity

definitions.note: the clue gives a noun; the answer is the adjective describing such a fat

indicators.note: talking means the parrot's name is heard spoken rather than spelt as usual

parts.note: Polly is the stock name for a pet parrot
unsaturated describes something able to take in more, with room to spare

explanation.surface: An overweight talking parrot that somehow has room for more.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talking' tells you POLLY is heard, giving POLY. 'Fat' stands for the kind of fat the adjective describes.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietary fat with several unsaturated bonds is called by this adjective, often used alone as a noun on food labels.

clue.text: It might be useful to lock up the cabinet …

definitions.text: It might be useful to lock up the cabinet …

parts.words: It might be useful to lock up the cabinet
parts.note: an asylum in the old sense locked up the mad; read the clue as a madhouse for a government's ministers rather than refuge granted to a dissident

explanation.surface: A suggestion that the whole government cabinet ought to be locked away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cabinet' makes the asylum political, and 'lock up' plays on the old sense of an asylum as a place for the insane.
explanation.definitionFit: This is refuge one country grants to someone fleeing persecution, punned here as a madhouse for politicians.

clue.text: … and secure English philosopher

parts.note: to secure a door is to lock it

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: lock up the cabinet, and keep an English thinker safe too.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the surface to 1 Down's locking up; it plays no part in the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: John Locke was a seventeenth-century English philosopher of empiricism and liberal government.

clue.text: To be frugal is futile

definitions.meaning: being frugal means to consume a smaller amount, split as two words
futile means pointless, of no worth

explanation.definitionFit: Read as two words it means to consume a smaller amount; as one word it means pointless or worthless.

clue.text: Lovesick suitor's first dismissal

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word suitor's

parts.note: to give a suitor the mitten is an old idiom for rejecting him

explanation.surface: A lovesick suitor faces his first rejection.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting the mitten' is an old idiom, chiefly American, for being turned down by a sweetheart.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone deeply infatuated is described as struck or smitten, the past participle of smite.

clue.text: Willing to put up picture collection

indicators.note: in a down clue up means the word for put is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to put something down is to set it
the Tate is the London gallery group holding a national art collection

explanation.surface: Someone happy to hang a set of paintings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Willing' is the adjective for having made a will, not eager. The TATE is Britain's national gallery of art in London.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies having made a valid will is described in law by this adjective.

clue.text: Soldiers pedal to avoid the dump

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to pedal is to cycle

explanation.surface: Troops riding bicycles to keep away from a rubbish heap.
explanation.definitionFit: Reprocessing waste for reuse keeps it out of landfill, the rubbish tip.

clue.text: Drummer boy with Ulster in former times

parts.note: Tim is a boy's name

indicators.note: in means one piece sits inside the word for former times

parts.note: former times is the past
NI, Northern Ireland, is often called Ulster

explanation.surface: A drummer boy from Ulster in days gone by.
explanation.definitionFit: An orchestral player of the kettledrums is a drummer by trade.

clue.text: Priest in bungled medical operation has a point

definitions.note: the clue gives a verb phrase; the answer is a noun describing something with a decimal point

indicators.note: bungled means messed up, so the letters of medical are jumbled

parts.note: Fr, Father, is the title of a Catholic priest
an operation is an action

explanation.surface: A clumsy surgical procedure involving a priest still makes some sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bungled' is the anagram signal and 'in' the container signal. The definition is a playful description: such a number is written with a point, not a sharp tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A number such as 0.25 is written with a dot, the decimal point, separating whole and part.

clue.text: Poet's legal process backed by wealth

definitions.note: Poet's is read as poet is, the 's linking definition to wordplay

parts.note: lucre is money or wealth, often filthy lucre

indicators.note: backed means the word for legal process is turned round

parts.note: a lawsuit is a legal process, a suit

explanation.surface: A poet goes to court with money behind him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns SUIT into TIUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucretius was a Roman poet, author of De Rerum Natura.

clue.text: Dot's follower, I see, sounding amusing

parts.note: in a web address dot is followed by com

indicators.note: sounding means the phrase I see is heard as two letters

parts.note: the phrase I see is spoken like the letters I and C

explanation.surface: Someone who follows Dot remarks that something is funny.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dot's' looks like a woman's name, but it is the dot of a dotcom address.
explanation.definitionFit: Something comic is funny or amusing, as in a comic turn.

clue.text: Free lunch, say, and chap going in on account of it

indicators.note: going in means the chap's word is put inside the other piece

parts.note: a free lunch is an example of a treat, hence say
a chap is a he, a male

explanation.surface: A free lunch, and a man arrives on the strength of it.
explanation.definitionFit: This old-fashioned adverb means because of that or on that account.

clue.text: A small volume of redirected mail gets hearty reception

parts.note: cc, cubic centimetre, is a small measure of volume

indicators.note: redirected mail is sent another way, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small amount of forwarded post earns a warm welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'redirected' rearranges MAIL into LAIM.
explanation.definitionFit: Acclaim is enthusiastic public praise, a hearty reception.

clue.text: Amphibian can be sinister if topped

indicators.note: topped means the word loses its first letter, its top

parts.note: sinister is Latin for left, used in heraldry

explanation.surface: A newt might seem menacing once its head is removed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' is not menacing here but its heraldic sense, left.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a young newt, an amphibian.

clue.text: Embarrassment caused by colour? No, the reverse

definitions.text: Embarrassment caused by colour? No, the reverse

parts.words: Embarrassment caused by colour? No, the reverse
parts.note: swap the phrase round: it is a colour caused by embarrassment, the deep red of a blush

explanation.surface: Someone wondering whether a colour can cause a blush.
explanation.definitionFit: This deep red is the shade a face turns when embarrassed.

clue.text: Pressing suit with the devil

parts.note: an imp is a little devil
a legal suit is an action

explanation.surface: Bringing a lawsuit with the devil's help.
explanation.walkthrough: 'suit' is a lawsuit, not clothing; IMP comes first despite the clue's order, as the devil goes with the suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Impaction is the act of pressing or packing something firmly in place.

clue.text: Pick out from the top twenty

indicators.note: out from means the letters come out of a run spanning the words top twenty

explanation.surface: Choosing something from the chart of the twenty best-selling records.
explanation.definitionFit: To opt is to choose or pick.

clue.text: Wind not half like crazy prophet

indicators.note: not half means half the letters of the word for wind are dropped

parts.note: a breeze is a light wind

indicators.note: crazy means the letters of like are scrambled

explanation.surface: A prophet who rants like a madman, full of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' drops BRE from BREEZE to give EZE; 'crazy' turns LIKE into KIEL.
explanation.definitionFit: Ezekiel is an Old Testament prophet with his own book.

clue.text: She translates 24

definitions.meaning: 24 Across is the French for life; the Greek word for life is a translation of it

explanation.definitionFit: Zoe is a girl's name, and also the Greek word for life, as vie is in French.

clue.text: Battle providing the French with entertainment

parts.note: le is French for the
panto, pantomime, is a British Christmas stage entertainment

explanation.surface: A battle staged in French as a pantomime.
explanation.walkthrough: PANTO is the British Christmas family show of slapstick and audience shouting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lepanto was the 1571 naval battle in which the Holy League beat the Ottoman fleet.

clue.text: Book of grayling between poles

indicators.note: between means the fish sits between the two poles

parts.note: the poles are north and south, N and S
umber is another name for the grayling fish

explanation.surface: A book about a grayling caught between two posts.
explanation.walkthrough: Note 'poles' gives both N and S, which the fish goes between.
explanation.definitionFit: Numbers is the fourth book of the Old Testament.

clue.text: Supervise lines in Old English

indicators.note: in means the lines sit inside the abbreviation for Old English

parts.note: lines of poetry are verse

explanation.surface: Checking over some lines written in Old English.
explanation.definitionFit: To oversee work is to supervise it.

clue.text: God put off with Middle East invasion

indicators.note: invasion means the Middle East forces its way inside the other word

parts.note: to deter is to put off

explanation.surface: A deity discouraged by an invasion of the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: Demeter is a goddess; 'God' is used of either sex in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Demeter is the Greek goddess of the harvest, a deity of the Olympian pantheon.

clue.text: Put down Dorset riot at the end of the day

indicators.note: a riot is disorder, so the letters of Dorset run wild
end of asks for the last letter of the word day

explanation.surface: Quelling a riot in the English county of Dorset at nightfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges DORSET into DESTRO. Dorset is a county in southern England.
explanation.definitionFit: To put down an animal or a rebellion is to destroy it.

clue.text: She's unusually mad about the country

definitions.note: read as she is; the definition is a woman's name

indicators.note: about means the jumbled letters go around the country
unusually means the letters of mad are arranged in an odd way

parts.note: Iran is a country

explanation.surface: A woman who is uncharacteristically angry about her country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unusually' rearranges MAD to M...DA, which goes 'about' IRAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Miranda is a woman's name, famously the heroine of The Tempest.

clue.text: Compete with life abroad

definitions.meaning: the French word for life, foreign to English

explanation.definitionFit: To vie is to compete; in French the same word means life.

clue.text: Late 10 becomes confused

definitions.note: 10 Across is comic; the definition names a comedian who has died

indicators.note: confused means the letters of becomes are jumbled

explanation.surface: A comedian from the past is getting muddled.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir Harry Secombe was a Welsh comedian and singer, one of the Goons on BBC radio, who died in 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Secombe was a much-loved comic performer, now dead.

clue.text: Spinning about orbits spinning

indicators.note: spinning means the letters of orbits whirl into a new order

parts.note: c, circa, is Latin for about

explanation.surface: Something whirling round orbits that are themselves rotating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spinning' at the end rearranges ORBITS into STROBI; C is circa.
explanation.definitionFit: Strobic describes something that appears to spin, as in a stroboscopic effect.

clue.text: Reared without a staple item

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the word for reared surrounds a

parts.note: an animal reared is bred

explanation.surface: Brought up without a basic foodstuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' looks like lacking, but it means outside here.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is a staple food, a basic item of the diet.

clue.text: Spanish river turning into the French one

indicators.note: into means the turned river goes inside the French article

parts.note: le is French for the

indicators.note: turning means the Spanish word is read backwards

parts.note: rio is Spanish for river

explanation.surface: A Spanish river flows round into a French one.
explanation.walkthrough: 'one' refers back to 'river': the answer is the French river.
explanation.definitionFit: The Loire is the longest river in France, the French river the clue refers to.

clue.text: It's almost cool to catch one east of Lake Victoria

indicators.note: almost means the last letter of the word for cool is dropped

parts.note: serene means calm or cool
to catch something is to get it
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Keeping cool while catching something in East Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: The Serengeti plains lie in Tanzania, east of Lake Victoria.

clue.text: Supposedly calm spot turned out nasty, with more danger

indicators.note: turned out means the letters of the fodder are reworked into a new form

explanation.surface: A place meant to be peaceful proved nasty and more dangerous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned out' rearranges NASTY, MORE and DANGER together; 'with' only joins them.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister garden tended by monks is the archetypal peaceful retreat, as in the light classic In a Monastery Garden.
